metadata.title: Week 10 Summary: HARNESS² Recursive Agent Harnessing

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Hrishikesh. In Week ten, we break down HARNESS squared from Northwestern University and Google Cloud AI Research: a recursive agent harnessing framework that evolves an agent's eight-component runtime scaffolding online without ground-truth verifiers.

props.command: analyze HARNESS² (arXiv:2610.14224): how coupled task-level and harnessing-level recursion evolve agent harnesses in an open world.
props.runningText: inspecting 8 runtime harness components and contrastive probes...
output: ✓ Agent = Frozen Model M + 8-File Execution Harness H (C1-C8)
✓ Up to +11.5 pts on WorkBuddy-Bench & +11.8 pp on Harvey LAB

beats.narration_text: An agent's capability depends as much on its runtime harness as on its frozen weights. Yet open-world tasks arrive without answer keys, and directly carrying a task-specific harness across shifting requirements causes noisy drift. HARNESS squared learns from the refinement process itself.

props.text:
Open-World Agent Hypothesis
Carry one mutated harness across every task
and rely on verifier scores to guide edits.
Wait, open-world streams have no verifiers.
HARNESS squared probes behavioral contrasts
and distills reusable library experience.
props.triggerWords: rely on verifier scores to guide edits

beats.narration_text: Examine the two coupled levels of recursion alongside the eight editable runtime files. Context files, on-demand skills, Python verification scripts, isolated subagents, and TypeScript middleware hooks are refined per task, while validated lessons update the continual improvement library.

How does task-level recursion guide edits without a grader? After sampling a reference trajectory, two scoped editors propose candidates: an Invariant editor targeting agentic workflow and tool errors, and a Domain editor encoding practitioner rules and artifact contracts.

beats.narration_text: In the JobBench producers case study, the base run scored forty-three point one because figures were never reconciled and spreadsheets were never reopened. Proposing a domain reconciliation skill plus verify outputs dot py lifted the composed re-run to seventy-seven point eight.

Across WorkBuddy-Bench, JobBench, and Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, a single contrastive step improves every model-harness configuration. On WorkBuddy-Bench, GLM-5 jumps eleven point five points in one step, surpassing base Gemini 3.5 Flash, while parallel recursion at k equals five reaches eighty point eight percent.

What happens if an editor rewrites the base harness directly without execution probes or the library? On WorkBuddy Code, direct editing crashes performance from seventy-three point four to sixty-three point two percent, whereas a k equals five experience library unlocks zero-shot gains.

props.text:
Harnessing-Level Ablation
Direct harness edits without execution probes
improve accuracy across unseen tasks.
Wait, blind editing drops Code by 10.2 points.
Accumulating an EXPERIENCE.md library at k=5
unlocks cross-task and cross-benchmark transfer.

beats.narration_text: Ablating HARNESS squared confirms every mechanism contributes: removing the experience library costs three point one points on WorkBuddy, removing scope splitting costs three point seven on JobBench, and removing on-demand skills costs five point three points, while tool errors drop up to thirty-seven percent.

HARNESS squared also succeeds when the same model serves as both executor and editor. In Claude Opus five self-improvement on JobBench, adding deliverable watchdog dot ts inside the C8 plugin hook stops runaway research and raises the score from seventy-two to one hundred.

Instead of bloating always-on system prompts, prefer on-demand skills, deterministic verification scripts, bounded subagents, and tool-loop plugins backed by behavioral contrasts. Audit your agent harness with this framework. Your turn.
